tex_content.html:
↗ lem:far-point-with-distant-antipode

If $D$ is at least the constant in the preceding lemma and $D\ge 32\sqrt{Q/3}T$, then $R_{g_\infty }(y,t)$ is uniformly bounded for $y\notin B(x_\infty ,0,D)$ and $t\in (-T,0]$. \end{claim}
Proof

↗ claim:distance-distortion-bound ↗ lem:far-point-with-distant-antipode \sketch Choose $z$ with $d_0(y,z)=d$ and $d_0(x_\infty ,z)>3d/2$. An unbounded curvature sequence at $y$ gives a small canonical neighborhood. If the two minimizing geodesics exit the same end, Toponogov and

\[ \cos \theta \ge 1-\frac{(4\pi \epsilon )^2}{2},\qquad d_t(x_\infty ,y),d_t(y,z)\le d+16\sqrt{Q/3}T \]

contradict $d_0(y,z)=d$ because $\epsilon <1/(8\pi )$. The neck alternative then separates $x_\infty $ and $z$ by balls of radius $4\pi R(y,t)^{-1/2}$; arbitrarily small such balls are impossible.

□
